title: Affine finitely presented relative Hom from a finite locally free source
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X\to S$ finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and $Y\to S$ affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and of finite presentation. Finite presentation means locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The functor on $S$-schemes $T$ sending $T$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_T(X\times_ST,Y\times_ST)$, with restriction by base change [def-pc-fibre-product], is represented by an affine $S$-scheme $H$ of finite presentation, with natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,H)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_T(X\times_ST,Y\times_ST)$ for all $T$. More explicitly, for every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$, the scheme $H\times_SU$ is isomorphic over $U$ to $\operatorname{Spec}P$ for a commutative $A$-algebra $P$ admitting a presentation $P\simeq A[z_1,\ldots,z_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$ with $n,m$ finite [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. No group structure on $X$ or $Y$ is assumed; zero and varying rank of $X\to S$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0BL3 (lemma-hom-from-finite-locally-free-into-affine) and Tag 05Y6 (lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine), coefficient construction with a finite presentation of the target algebra. The finitely presented refinement is Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Lemma 2.1.3, first assertion, printed pp.58-59; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $p:X\to S$. By finite local freeness, $p$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. The pushforward $p_*\mathcal O_X$ is locally a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathcal O_S$ by [lem-sc-finite-pushforward-locally-free]. Refine its trivializing open cover by affine opens using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. For each resulting $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, finiteness and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a),(b) give $X_i=X\times_SU_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. Restricting the trivialization to $U_i$ and taking sections gives an $R_i$-basis of $B_i$ of some finite size $d_i$: sections of a finite direct sum are tuples of sections. The numbers $d_i$ may differ; zero is allowed. The fibre product is the inverse-image open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 02KB, lemma-finite-flat; choice of finite-free affine charts in Tag 0BL3, more-morphisms.tex, lemma-hom-from-finite-locally-free-into-affine; Tag 01IT, schemes.tex, lemma-basis-affine-opens

proof.text: Affineness of $Y\to S$ gives $Y_i=Y\times_SU_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$. It is the inverse-image open in $Y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to the affine opens $Y_i\subseteq Y$ and $U_i\subseteq S$. Its locally finite presentation hypothesis is part of the assumed finite presentation of $Y\to S$. Thus, writing $R,B,C,d$ for one chart, choose a finite presentation $C=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ and an $R$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $B$. No Noetherian hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize, (1) implies (2); finite-presentation specialization of the presentation in Tag 05Y6, more-morphisms.tex, lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine

proof.text: Set $E=B[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$, where coefficients are mapped from $R$ to $B$. The canonical $B$-algebra isomorphism $E\simeq B\otimes_RC$ is obtained directly from the two universal properties. One map sends $b$ to $b\otimes1$ and $x_i$ to $1\otimes\bar x_i$; it descends since each $f_k$ vanishes in $C$. For the inverse use $B\to E$ and the $R$-algebra map $C\to E$ sending $\bar x_i$ to $[x_i]$. The latter is well-defined since each $f_k$ is zero in $E$; quotient classes with the same representative difference in the generated ideal have the same value. The tensor universal property gives $b\otimes c\mapsto b[c]$. The composites fix $B$ and all $x_i$, respectively both tensor factors, so polynomial uniqueness and tensor uniqueness make them identities.

source.place: Tag 05Y6, lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine, coefficient construction; elementary scalar extension of the displayed target presentation

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-finite-free-algebra-map-coordinates] with base ring $R$, finite free algebra $B$, and the presented $B$-algebra $E$. It constructs
$$Q=R[a_{ij}:1\le i\le n,1\le j\le d],\qquad P=Q/(c_{kj}:1\le k\le m,1\le j\le d),$$
where the $c_{kj}$ are the coefficients of $f_k(\sum_j e_j\otimes a_{1j},\ldots,\sum_j e_j\otimes a_{nj})$. Its natural bijection is $\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-alg}}(P,A)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{B\text{-alg}}(E,B\otimes_RA)$. Via Step 3 the latter set is $\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-alg}}(C,B\otimes_RA)$: restrict along $c\mapsto1\otimes c$; the inverse extends by $b\otimes c\mapsto(b\otimes1)h(c)$. Tensor uniqueness makes these inverse, and the formulas commute with every map $A\to A'$. There are $nd$ variables and $md$ displayed relations, both finite, so $P$ has the finite presentation required in the item, after numbering these two finite families.

source.place: Tag 05Y6, lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine, displayed polynomial algebra and coefficient ideal; finite n,m specialization

proof.text: Let $H_i=\operatorname{Spec}P$ on this chart. For an affine test $T=\operatorname{Spec}A\to U_i$, the universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $X_T=X\times_ST\simeq X_i\times_{U_i}T$ and $Y_T\simeq Y_i\times_{U_i}T$, since $T\to S$ factors through $U_i$ and $X_i=X\times_SU_i$, $Y_i=Y\times_SU_i$. Then [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $X_T$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_RA)$ and $Y_T$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_RA)$. Spectrum's contravariant Hom bijection and the tensor universal property identify $\operatorname{Hom}_T(X_T,Y_T)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-alg}}(C,B\otimes_RA)$. Explicitly, the $A$-algebra map $C\otimes_RA\to B\otimes_RA$ corresponding to $h$ sends $c\otimes a$ to $h(c)(1\otimes a)$; restricting to $c\otimes1$ is the inverse. Step 4 and spectrum now give $\operatorname{Hom}_{U_i}(T,H_i)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_T(X_T,Y_T)$ naturally on affine tests. At $A=P$, the identity gives a universal relative morphism $b_i:X_{H_i}\to Y_{H_i}$. The coordinate formulas show that the bijection on any affine test is pullback of $b_i$.

source.place: Tag 05Y6, lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine, universal relative morphism and the inverse on affine tests

proof.text: The same universal morphism gives the bijection on every $U_i$-scheme $T$. Cover $T$ by affine opens $T_a$. Given $b:X_T\to Y_T$ over $T$, use Step 5 on each $T_a$ to obtain $g_a:T_a\to H_i$. On an intersection $T_a\cap T_b$, take an affine open cover; naturality of Step 5 identifies both restricted maps with the restriction of $b$ there. Injectivity on these affine tests, followed by morphism-gluing uniqueness, makes $g_a$ and $g_b$ agree on the whole intersection. The maps $g_a$ therefore glue uniquely to $g:T\to H_i$. Its composite to $U_i$ is the structural map, since this holds on the cover. Pullback of $b_i$ along $g$ equals $b$ on the inverse-image open cover $X_{T_a}$ of $X_T$, hence globally. Conversely, applying these constructions to a map $g$ recovers $g$ on all $T_a$, hence recovers $g$. All maps to $Y_T$ are over $T$ because that equality of composites can also be checked on this cover. Pulling back along an arbitrary $T'\to T$ commutes with pulling back $b_i$; uniqueness of the inverse then proves naturality for every map of tests. No intersection was assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 05Y6, lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine, extension from affine tests; schemes.tex, Tag 01JA, section-glueing-schemes, and Tag 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product

proof.text: For $U_{ij}=U_i\cap U_j$, the two restrictions $H_i\times_SU_{ij}$ and $H_j\times_SU_{ij}$ represent the same functor on $U_{ij}$-schemes: by the fibre-product universal property a map into either restriction is a map into the corresponding $H_i$ or $H_j$ over the prescribed base. Step 6 identifies both with relative morphisms $X_T\to Y_T$. The identity of this functor gives a unique transition isomorphism by [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection]. Its inverse comes from the reverse identity; the diagonal transition and every triple-overlap composite are identities by Yoneda injectivity. This uses all-test representability, so the overlaps need not be affine. Apply [lem-galois-glue] to obtain an $S$-scheme $H$ and compatible isomorphisms $H\times_SU_i\simeq H_i$.

source.place: Tag 0BL3, lemma-hom-from-finite-locally-free-into-affine, base-chart gluing; schemes.tex, Tag 01JB, lemma-glue, and Tag 01JC, lemma-glue-schemes

proof.text: For any $S$-scheme $T$, the inverse-image opens $T_i=T\times_SU_i$ cover $T$. A relative morphism $b:X_T\to Y_T$ gives maps $T_i\to H_i\to H$ by Step 6. On overlaps these agree by the definition of the transitions in Step 7, so morphism gluing gives a unique $S$-map $T\to H$. Conversely an $S$-map $T\to H$ restricts to maps $T_i\to H_i$, giving relative morphisms on $X_{T_i}$. Their composites to $Y_T$ agree on overlaps, hence glue to a map $X_T\to Y_T$ over $T$. These two operations are inverse by local uniqueness. The local bijections commute with every pullback of tests by Step 6, and gluing uniqueness makes the global bijections natural. This establishes exactly the functor and the base-change restriction maps in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0BL3, lemma-hom-from-finite-locally-free-into-affine, gluing of relative morphisms; schemes.tex, Tag 01JA, section-glueing-schemes

proof.text: The affine open cover $(U_i)$ of $S$ has affine inverse images: the inverse image of $U_i$ in $H$ is $H\times_SU_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], which is isomorphic over $U_i$ to $H_i$ by Step 7. Thus [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] makes $H\to S$ affine. Each $H_i=\operatorname{Spec}P_i\to\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ is locally of finite presentation by the definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], since the whole affine source and target themselves provide the required neighbourhoods at every point and Step 4 gives a finite ring presentation. Target-open locality [lem-sfb-separated-lfp-target-open-locality] gives local finite presentation of $H\to S$. Affine-morphism permanence supplies quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence quasi-separatedness, so $H\to S$ is of finite presentation under the convention in the item.

source.place: Tag 01S8, lemma-characterize-affine; Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize, (3) implies (1); affine quasi-compactness and separatedness, Tag 01S7, lemma-affine-separated

proof.text: Finally take any affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$, without requiring a basis of $X_U$ on all of $U$. Affineness makes the inverse-image open $H_U$ affine, say $H_U=\operatorname{Spec}P$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to the affine opens $H_U\subset H$ and $U\subset S$ for the locally finitely presented map $H\to S$ established in Step 9. It gives $P\simeq A[z_1,\ldots,z_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$ with finite $n,m$, exactly the additional explicit clause. If $d_i=0$, then $B_i=0$ and $E=0$; the coefficient lemma used in Step 4 explicitly gives $P_i=R_i$. Thus $H_i=U_i$ and every test has the unique morphism from its empty source. If $X=S$, a rank-one basis identifies the construction with $Y$. Empty test schemes, empty generator or relation families, and an empty base are included by the same universal properties and gluing uniqueness. Nothing imposed positive or constant global rank, or a group structure.
